steps.notes: Literal implementation of the given F_xx/F_xy formulas passes all 3 tests (joint and isolate). Formulas verified self-consistent with the dyadic Green's function derivation. Cosmetic: test powers P=1e7..1e9 W are unphysical for tweezers but harmless; effective tolerance is atol-dominated (~0.5% relative on ~2e-6 N targets) but no plausible wrong impl slips through.

Passes ONLY with non-literal interpretations: differentiation step must be relative (dx = h*distance, or analytic dF/dR), and trap stiffness k_i = alpha*E_i^2/w^2 must be derived from off-prompt physics. Literal central difference with step h=1e-6 m fails all 3 tests (wrong sign and magnitude). See findings.

Straightforward RK4 per the given update equations passes all 4 tests (joint and isolate). Dynamics only see eigenvalue differences (~1e4 rad/s), so 1e5 steps is fully converged: exact expm solution and 2x-steps RK4 also pass tests 1-3. dt=t0/steps is the natural reading; a linspace-style dt=t0/(steps-1) with `steps` updates overshoots t0 and fails (rel err 8e-4), but that is a solver bug, not a data defect. Test 4 alone would pass a no-op (nf=n0) implementation, but tests 1-3 constrain the step, so no D8 mis-score. NOTE: a solver whose 32.2 used the literal-h reading also fails ALL of 32.3 (its tests build H via the solver's generate_Hamiltonian) - the 32.2 defect cascades.

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'h : float  Step size of the differentiation'; tests pass h = 1e-6. Every other length input is in meters (R=1.55e-6, l=1550e-9, w=600e-9, a=100e-9), so the literal reading is an absolute step of 1e-6 m in R. But k*h = (2pi/1550e-9)*1e-6 = 4.05 rad: the step spans more than half an optical period, so any finite difference with it is meaningless. Measured (test 0, pair distance d=R): literal central diff (F(d+h)-F(d-h))/(2h) = +3.970e-9, literal forward diff = +1.837e-8, while the target encodes k_01 = -7.682875e-08 -- the EXACT analytic derivative dF/dR (matches a central difference with relative step dx = h*d, i.e. ~1.5e-12 m, to all 7 backed-out digits on all 12 (i,j,test) combinations). steptest verdicts: literal-h implementation FAILS 32.2 3/3 (off-diagonals wrong in sign and magnitude, e.g. mine -180.0 vs target +3519.9) and consequently FAILS 32.3 4/4 (its tests call the solver's generate_Hamiltonian with h=1e-6); relative-step implementation PASSES 32.2 3/3 and 32.3 4/4. Pass window: any absolute step <= ~2 nm (need (k*dx)^2/6 < 1e-5) or analytic differentiation passes; the docstring's literal value is ~5e5 times too large.
findings.suggested_fix: State the convention in the docstring/background, e.g. 'h : relative step size; the finite-difference step used at inter-particle distance R_ij is h*R_ij', or keep absolute semantics and change the test inputs to h = 1e-12. Alternatively specify k_ij as the analytic derivative and drop h.

findings.evidence: The background defines Omega_i = sqrt((k_i + sum_{j!=i} k_ij)/m) but never defines the trap stiffness k_i -- it appears only as an undefined symbol ('m x_i'' + k_i x_i + ...'). No prompt text (main description, step 1 or 2 background, docstrings) gives the tweezer stiffness. Backing it out of the h5 target (test 0, center particle): k_i_implied = 1.0938856634857722e-05 N/m vs alpha*E0^2/w^2 = 1.0938856634857214e-05 (13-digit match), with E0 = sqrt(4P/(pi w^2 eps0 c)) from step 1's background. The solver must independently supply the harmonic expansion of the Gaussian-tweezer dipole potential U(x) = -(1/4) alpha E0^2 exp(-2x^2/w^2) => k = alpha E0^2/w^2. This is standard levitated-optomechanics physics but entirely absent from the problem; the common factor-of-2 convention slips (U = -(1/2) alpha E^2 with amplitude vs RMS field, or exp(-x^2/w^2) amplitude profile) give k_i off by 2x and hence the H diagonal off by sqrt(2) (1.397e6 vs target 9.820e5) -- a gross failure under np.allclose. (m = rho*(4/3)*pi*a^3 is also unstated but unambiguous.)
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 2 background: 'Each tweezer contributes a transverse trap stiffness k_i = alpha E_i^2 / w^2 (harmonic expansion of the dipole potential U = -(1/4) alpha E_i^2 exp(-2x^2/w^2)), and the nanosphere mass is m = (4/3) pi a^3 rho.'

findings.evidence: Test 4 asserts abs(sum(nf) - sum(n0)) < 1e-6 with sum(n0) = 39550742.17, i.e. it demands the RK4 trace be conserved to 2.5e-14 RELATIVE (about 134 ulp of the sum) across 100000 steps -- a pure roundoff-accumulation quantity, not a property the spec can guarantee. Measured drift across 7 reasonable implementation variants (operator association orders, np.dot vs @, grouped/k-divided accumulation): 5.96e-8 to 3.20e-7, so the worst variant passes with only a 3.1x margin. All variants pass on this platform (numpy 2.2.6, x86-64), but a different BLAS/architecture/summation order could plausibly exceed the absolute 1e-6 bound. (Also note: this test alone is satisfied by a no-op nf = n0 implementation -- (True, True) -- but tests 1-3 of the same step are strongly discriminating, so no false positive at step granularity.)
findings.suggested_fix: Loosen the conservation bound to something roundoff-safe at this magnitude, e.g. abs(diff)/sum(n0) < 1e-12 or abs(diff) < 1e-3, or compare the full nf vector to a frozen target like the other tests.

overall_assessment: Steps 32.1 and 32.3 are fair and were reproduced exactly from the prompt text (32.1 formulas verified self-consistent; 32.3's mandated RK4 is fully converged, so even exact-propagator solutions pass). Step 32.2 is the problem: the differentiation step h is documented as an absolute 'step size' but the target requires a relative step h*R_ij (or the analytic derivative) -- the literal reading fails 32.2 AND cascades to fail all of 32.3 -- and the trap stiffness k_i = alpha*E^2/w^2 that sets the Hamiltonian diagonal is never stated anywhere. A competent solver passes only by recognizing the literal h is physically nonsensical and by independently deriving standard tweezer physics, so 2 of 3 scored steps hinge on guessing/recovering unstated author choices.
